name: Chip company (category)
description: A company that designs chips and sells them under its own name, or designs them for its own products. It is the 'seller' counted in the headline chip-market statistics.

name: Integrated device manufacturer (IDM) (category)
description: A chip company that designs its chips and also makes, packages and tests them in its own factories.

name: Memory chip maker (category)
description: An IDM that makes commodity-like memory chips (DRAM, NAND flash, HBM); prices swing hard with the cycle and are set in periodically renegotiated agreements.

name: Fabless chip company (category)
description: A chip company that designs and sells chips but owns no fab; it pays foundries to make wafers and OSATs to package and test them.

name: System company designing its own chips (category)
description: A cloud provider or device maker that designs custom chips for its own products or data centres (e.g. hyperscaler CPUs and AI chips) rather than for sale on the open market.

name: Design-enablement provider (category)
description: A company that supplies what chip designers need to design: software, licensed design blocks or design services.

name: EDA vendor (category)
description: Sells electronic design automation (EDA) software used to design and verify chips, mostly as time-based licences.

name: Semiconductor IP licensor (category)
description: Licenses reusable, pre-designed chip blocks (e.g. processor cores, interfaces) for a licence fee and often a royalty on every chip shipped.

name: Design-service / ASIC house (category)
description: Takes a customer's chip from specification to finished product, doing design work and managing the foundry and packaging steps (also called a design house or turnkey ASIC provider).

name: Device-level patent licensor (category)
description: Licenses patents to device makers (not design blocks to chip designers) for a royalty based on the device's selling price.

name: Contract manufacturing-service provider (category)
description: A company that manufactures, packages, tests or makes masks for chips designed by others.

name: Foundry (category)
description: A contract chip manufacturer: it makes wafers to its customers' designs using its own processes.

name: Pure-play foundry (category)
description: A foundry that only manufactures for customers and does not sell chips of its own design.

name: IDM foundry business (category)
description: A foundry business run inside a company that also designs and sells its own chips (an IDM offering spare or dedicated capacity to outside customers).

name: OSAT (outsourced assembly and test) (category)
description: A contractor that cuts, packages and tests chips for IDMs and fabless companies; the customer usually keeps title to the wafers.

name: Photomask maker (category)
description: Makes photomasks (the patterned plates used in lithography) from each customer's design, either as an independent 'merchant' shop or a 'captive' shop inside a chipmaker.

name: Upstream supplier to fabs (category)
description: A supplier of the tools, materials, chemicals, gases and software that fabs and packaging plants consume.

name: Semiconductor equipment maker (category)
description: Builds the machines used to make and test chips, and earns a large share of revenue from servicing and upgrading its installed base.

name: Wafer-fab (front-end) equipment maker (category)
description: Makes front-end tools: lithography, deposition, etch, implant, polishing (CMP), metrology and inspection.

name: Test-equipment maker (category)
description: Makes automatic test equipment used at wafer probe, final test and system-level test; sells to IDMs, fabless firms, foundries and OSATs.

name: Semiconductor materials supplier (category)
description: Supplies the consumable materials of chipmaking: wafers, photoresists, chemicals, gases, photomask blanks and packaging materials.

name: Silicon wafer / polysilicon supplier (category)
description: Grows ultra-pure silicon and slices and polishes it into the wafers that chips are built on.

name: Process-chemical / photoresist supplier (category)
description: Supplies photoresists, wet chemicals and etchants used in the fab.

name: Specialty-gas producer and purifier (category)
description: Produces and purifies gases such as neon used in lithography lasers and other process steps.

name: Packaging-materials / IC-substrate supplier (category)
description: Makes the substrates (e.g. ABF), lead frames, bonding wire and other materials that chips are packaged with.

name: Critical-mineral producer (category)
description: Produces raw minerals such as gallium, germanium or rare earths that are refined into chip materials; production is geographically concentrated.

name: Manufacturing-software vendor (category)
description: Sells factory software such as manufacturing execution systems (MES), fault detection and yield management to fabs and packaging plants.

name: Channel intermediary (category)
description: A company that resells chips between chipmakers and buyers.

name: Authorized (franchised) distributor (category)
description: Buys chips from chipmakers under franchise agreements and resells them to device makers, adding design support, programming and logistics.

name: Independent distributor / broker (category)
description: Resells chips outside the chipmakers' authorized channels (the 'open market'), where provenance is not assured and counterfeits can enter.

name: Chip buyer (category)
description: A company that buys chips to build into products.

name: OEM / device maker (category)
description: An original equipment manufacturer that designs and sells end products (computers, phones, cars, industrial equipment) containing chips.

name: EMS provider (category)
description: An electronics manufacturing services contractor that assembles chips onto boards and systems for OEMs.

name: Capital provider (category)
description: A party that finances chip companies or fabs (equity, co-investment, loans).

name: Financial co-investor in fabs (category)
description: A financial partner that co-funds a chipmaker's fab construction in exchange for a minority stake in the fab or its output.

name: Integrated circuit (IC)
description: Many transistors and other components built on one piece of semiconductor; about 88% of chip sales.

name: Logic IC
description: Chips that compute or control (processors, accelerators, custom logic); the largest WSTS category.

name: AI accelerator / advanced computing chip
description: Processors built for AI training and inference in data centres; the target of US export controls and the Section 232 tariff.

name: Memory IC
description: Chips that store data (DRAM, NAND flash, HBM and others).

name: DRAM
description: Dynamic random-access memory: fast working memory, made by a handful of IDMs.

name: High-bandwidth memory (HBM)
description: Stacks of DRAM dies joined by through-silicon vias, packaged next to AI processors.

name: NAND flash
description: Non-volatile storage memory, now built in 3D stacks of hundreds of layers.

name: Analog IC
description: Chips that handle real-world signals and power (amplifiers, converters, drivers).

name: Micro IC (MPU/MCU/DSP)
description: Microprocessors, microcontrollers and digital signal processors, as grouped by WSTS.

name: Discrete semiconductor
description: Single-function devices such as transistors, diodes and thyristors.

name: Optoelectronics
description: Devices that emit or detect light (LEDs, image sensors, laser diodes); excludes LCD panels.

name: Sensors and actuators
description: Semiconductor sensors (pressure, motion, magnetic etc.) and actuators.

name: Computing / AI end market
description: PCs, servers and data-centre/AI systems; the largest end use.

name: Communications end market
description: Phones and network equipment.

name: Consumer end market
description: Consumer electronics other than PCs and phones.

name: Automotive end market
description: Chips in cars and vehicles.

name: Industrial end market
description: Factory, energy, medical and other industrial equipment.

name: Government / military end market
description: Public-sector and defence uses; WSTS groups military inside Government.

name: Pre-competitive research
description: University, consortium and company research that precedes product design.

name: Chip design
description: Specification, logic design, physical design and verification of a chip, using EDA software and licensed IP.

name: Wafer production
description: Growing silicon ingots and slicing and polishing them into wafers.

name: Mask making
description: Turning each finished design into a set of photomasks, one per layer.

name: Wafer fabrication (front end)
description: Building circuits on wafers in a fab through hundreds of repeated process steps.

name: Assembly, packaging and test (back end)
description: Testing dies on the wafer, cutting them apart, packaging them and testing again.

name: Distribution
description: Moving finished chips to buyers, directly or through distributors and the open market.

name: System integration
description: Mounting chips on boards and building end products (EMS providers and OEMs).

name: DUV lithography
description: Deep-ultraviolet lithography, including immersion DUV (water between lens and wafer); lasers use neon-containing excimer gas.

name: EUV lithography (0.33 NA)
description: Extreme-ultraviolet lithography at 13.5 nm wavelength using mirrors in vacuum; one supplier makes the scanners; needed at 7 nm and below.

name: High-NA EUV lithography (0.55 NA)
description: Next-generation EUV with 0.55 numerical aperture and 8 nm resolution; high-volume use expected from 2027.

name: FinFET transistor
description: A 3D fin-shaped transistor introduced in 2011 by Intel; still the mainstream leading-edge transistor before gate-all-around.

name: Gate-all-around (nanosheet) transistor
description: Transistor whose gate wraps the channel on all sides; in production at 3 nm/2 nm class; key to scaling below 3 nm.

name: Backside power delivery
description: Routing power through the back of the wafer to free front-side wiring (e.g. PowerVia, Super Power Rail).

name: 2.5D interposer packaging
description: Placing several dies (e.g. a processor and HBM stacks) side by side on a silicon or organic interposer (e.g. CoWoS).

name: 3D stacking and hybrid bonding
description: Stacking dies directly on top of each other with very fine-pitch bonds (e.g. SoIC).

name: Chiplets
description: Building a system from several small dies assembled close together instead of one large chip; improves yield but needs known-good-die testing.

name: Glass package substrates
description: Glass core substrates proposed to replace organic substrates for large packages (announced, not yet in volume per evidence).

name: 300 mm silicon wafer
description: The standard wafer size for advanced fabs; 99.7% of capacity at 45 nm or below.

name: Gallium nitride (GaN) wafers
description: A wide-bandgap material used for power and RF chips, now moving to 300 mm wafers.

name: Process node naming
description: The generational label ('7 nm', '3 nm') attached to a manufacturer's process; not a physical measurement.

name: Process design kit (PDK)
description: The foundry's rulebook and parts kit for one process: design rules, device models, cell libraries and EDA tech files.

name: Layout database (GDSII / OASIS)
description: The final geometric layout of a chip handed over at tape-out, in GDSII or OASIS format.

name: Mask set
description: The set of photomasks for one design, one per patterned layer.

name: WAT / PCM data
description: Electrical test results from test structures on each wafer; one of the few data types foundries routinely share with customers.

name: Wafer / substrate map
description: Die-by-die pass/fail (bin) map passed from wafer sort to assembly and final test.

name: Test result data (STDF)
description: Per-lot, per-wafer, per-part test results from testers, commonly in STDF format.

name: Equipment sensor data (FDC)
description: Readings from the 100-200 sensors on each process tool, used for fault detection and classification.

name: Demand forecasts and orders
description: Forecasts, orders and allocations exchanged between device makers, chip companies and manufacturers; format and systems not yet evidenced.

name: Manufacturing execution system (MES)
description: Software that runs the fab: tracks lots, WIP, recipes, masks and equipment status, and keeps genealogy.

name: Fault detection and classification (FDC) system
description: Software that watches tool sensor data to catch process faults.

name: Foundry customer portal
description: Online system through which a foundry receives tape-outs and gives customers lot status, yield and WAT data (e.g. TSMC-Online).

name: SEMI E30 GEM / SECS
description: The standard for how semiconductor equipment talks to the factory host system.

name: SEMI E142 substrate mapping
description: Standard data items for wafer and substrate maps from wafer through assembly to final test.

name: SEMI P39 OASIS
description: Layout interchange format that succeeded GDSII Stream.

name: Standard Test Data Format (STDF)
description: Common format for semiconductor test results, originated by Teradyne.

name: JEDEC HBM4 (JESD270-4)
description: JEDEC memory standard for fourth-generation HBM: up to 2 TB/s and 16-high stacks.

name: UCIe die-to-die interconnect
description: Consortium standard for connecting chiplets from different suppliers inside one package.

name: WSTS world semiconductor market statistics
description: Monthly and forecast chip sales by product and region compiled from member reports; the source of the headline market size.

name: SEMI equipment billings statistics
description: Equipment billings compiled from SEMI and SEAJ member data.

name: SEMI materials market statistics
description: Annual semiconductor materials revenue split into fab and packaging materials.

name: ESD Alliance design-industry revenue
description: Quarterly revenue of EDA, semiconductor IP and design services.

name: ISIC Rev.4 class 2610
description: UN industry class 'Manufacture of electronic components and boards', wider than chips.

name: NAICS 334410
description: North American industry 'Semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing', also wider than chips.

name: HS headings 8541/8542
description: Customs headings for semiconductor devices and integrated circuits.

name: Long-term capacity / supply agreement
description: Multi-year agreements with volume commitments and reserved capacity (foundry) or periodically renegotiated pricing (memory).

name: Customer capacity prepayment
description: Advance payments by customers to reserve foundry capacity or secure supply.

name: IP licence fee plus per-chip royalty
description: Multi-year licence fees plus a royalty on every chip containing the IP.

name: Device-level patent royalty
description: A percentage of the device's wholesale price, paid quarterly by device makers.

name: EDA time-based licence
description: Time-based network licences bundled with support, plus some upfront licences and maintenance.

name: Franchised distribution agreement (price protection)
description: Supplier agreements that protect distributors against price erosion and obsolescence.

name: Consigned-wafer OSAT agreement
description: Customer keeps title to wafers; no binding volumes; customer bears unused materials.

name: Installed-base service subscription
description: Service, spares and upgrades for installed tools, largely subscriptions.

name: Milestone-based grant and investment tax credit
description: Grants reimbursed on project milestones, loans, investment tax credits with direct pay, and state equity.

name: US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
description: US Commerce Department bureau that writes and enforces the Export Administration Regulations, including chip and equipment controls and the Entity List.

name: CHIPS Program Office (US Commerce / NIST)
description: Runs the CHIPS Act manufacturing incentives; placed under the US Investment Accelerator in March 2025.

name: US Department of the Treasury
description: Administers the Outbound Investment Security Program; the IRS (part of Treasury) administers the 48D credit.

name: Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR)
description: Runs Section 301 trade investigations and actions, including on Chinese semiconductors.

name: US President (Section 232 proclamations)
description: Imposes national-security tariffs under Section 232 by proclamation after a Commerce investigation.

name: US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
description: Requires Form SD conflict-minerals disclosure from reporting companies.

name: US Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
description: Sued to block Nvidia's acquisition of Arm (abandoned 2022).

name: US DMEA Trusted Supplier Program
description: Defense Microelectronics Activity accreditation of trusted suppliers for sensitive ICs.

name: European Commission
description: Proposes EU chip law (Chips Act, Chips Act 2.0), approves State aid and updates the EU dual-use list.

name: European Chemicals Agency (ECHA)
description: EU agency running the REACH PFAS restriction process; effect on fabs not yet established.

name: Netherlands Minister for Foreign Trade and Development
description: Issues the Dutch national export licences for advanced chipmaking equipment.

name: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
description: Controls chipmaking-equipment exports under FEFTA and runs Japan's chip subsidy programme.

name: China Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
description: Licenses critical-mineral exports and runs trade-remedy investigations (e.g. anti-dumping on US analog ICs).

name: China Cybersecurity Review Office (CAC)
description: Conducted the 2023 cybersecurity review of Micron products.

name: China National IC Industry Investment Fund (Big Fund)
description: State-backed equity fund for the chip industry; phase III registered 2024 with CNY 344bn.

name: Taiwan MOEA International Trade Administration
description: Maintains Taiwan's Strategic High-Tech Commodities entity list.

name: South Korea National Assembly
description: Passed the K-Chips Act tax-credit amendment (2025) and the Semiconductor Special Act (2026).

name: India Semiconductor Mission (MeitY)
description: Runs the Semicon India incentive programme and ISM 2.0.

name: Wassenaar Arrangement
description: 42-state regime keeping a common dual-use control list implemented in national law.

name: UN Statistics Division (ISIC)
description: Maintains the ISIC industry classification.

name: World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS)
description: Non-profit of chip companies that compiles the reference chip-sales statistic from member reports.

name: Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA)
description: US trade body that publishes WSTS-based monthly sales and value-chain studies.

name: SEMI
description: Global association of equipment and materials suppliers; publishes equipment/materials statistics and runs the SEMI Standards programme.

name: Semiconductor Equipment Association of Japan (SEAJ)
description: Contributes member data to SEMI's equipment statistics.

name: ESD Alliance
description: SEMI technology community that reports electronic system design (EDA and IP) industry revenue.

name: Global Semiconductor Alliance (formerly Fabless Semiconductor Association)
description: Founded 1994 to promote the fabless model; renamed 2007.

name: JEDEC Solid State Technology Association
description: Develops open memory, packaging and ESD standards; 380+ members.

name: UCIe Consortium
description: Consortium that maintains the UCIe chiplet interconnect specification.

name: SEMATECH
description: US government-industry R&D consortium formed in 1987.

name: Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI)
description: Taiwan's state research institute; spun off UMC (1980) and TSMC (1987).

name: imec
description: Belgian research centre working on 3D integration, hybrid bonding and chiplets.
